name: Oscilloscope
summary: Instrument that displays the waveform of a signal against time, drawn with a waveform inside the instrument outline.
description: An oscilloscope displays how a voltage or current changes over time. In drawings it appears in test set-ups, laboratory panels and commissioning procedures, with its probe points shown so readers know exactly where waveforms are to be captured.

The symbol does not show probe type or reference. Connecting an earth-referenced scope ground lead to a live point in a power circuit can short the circuit, so differential probes or isolated channels must be specified in the procedure rather than assumed from the symbol.
readingNotes: Identify the probe reference point for each channel.
Check whether differential probes are required.
distinction: An oscilloscope shows a waveform shape; a disturbance recorder stores triggered records for later analysis.

facts.label: Main risk
facts.value: Earth-referenced probe leads on live circuits
